supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:20 UTC, ivy.chen ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon recorded creation of that archive four seconds later.
At 13:50:50 UTC, the proxy recorded 51,000,000 client-to-server bytes from WS-ICHEN-01 to quickshare-drop.net, and Zeek recorded 51,000,389 originating bytes for the corresponding proxy connection.
The transfer was made through Chrome running as ivy.chen; the endpoint network event identifies Chrome PID 4120 connecting to the proxy on the matching source port.

The archive creation and the large outbound transfer occurred about five minutes apart, and the transfer destination is not among the organization’s approved sharing or cloud-storage services. This strongly supports suspected exfiltration of the archived client data, although the logs do not prove that c.zip was the exact uploaded payload.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and Zeek records establish destination and approximate transfer volume, but do not expose the uploaded filename or content. Records: T059-00174, T059-00175.

The process and file records show archive creation, while the network records show Chrome’s proxy connection; the available records do not directly link the archive file to that connection. Records: T059-00102, T059-00104, T059-00177.
The supplied evidence does not establish whether the transfer had specific business authorization.
claims_not_established: That c.zip was definitively the file uploaded to quickshare-drop.net.
The content, sensitivity, or ownership of the transferred data.
Whether ivy.chen intended to exfiltrate data or had an undocumented exception or authorization.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and inspect c.zip, including its hash, size, and contents; preserve the endpoint and relevant browser artifacts.
Collect browser upload history, destination-side or proxy upload details, and DLP records that could identify the uploaded object and confirm whether it was c.zip.
Review FILE-NWD-01 share permissions and access auditing for the files under Shared\Clients around 13:45 UTC.
Confirm with ivy.chen and the relevant data owner whether this transfer was authorized, and check for any documented exception.
unrelated_findings: A Dropbox updater service process ran on WS-ICHEN-01; Dropbox is not listed among approved services. This is separate from the alerted quickshare-drop.net transfer. Records: T059-00011, T059-00013.
The workstation accessed Google account sign-in pages in Chrome. This is outside the alerted transfer and should be reviewed separately if relevant. Records: T059-00139, T059-00140, T059-00152.
The workstation accessed the AWS console in Chrome, which is not listed among approved services. This is separate from the alerted transfer. Records: T059-00212, T059-00213, T059-00222.

DC-NWD-01 recorded a Kerberos ticket request for ivy.chen from WS-NBLAKE-01’s address, followed by a successful network logon for ivy.chen on WS-NBLAKE-01. This is a separate cross-host account-use finding and does not establish a connection to the alerted upload. Records: T059-00248, T059-00249, T059-00250.
